what_happened.what: Justin and magent build Message.from_json() (later renamed from_jsonl_claude_code_v2), a classmethod that dedupes by UUID and instantiates the correct polymorphic Message subtype, moving import logic out of the import script and into models.py, shrinking the import script's message-processing loop from ~230 to 26 lines.

Same pattern extended to CompactingAction.from_jsonl_claude_code_v2() with hash-based deterministic IDs; RawImportedContent storage added for both Messages and CompactingActions so orphaned data can be inspected via raw JSONL in the Memory Lane UI.

Added preceding_message FK to CompactingAction so every compact can trace back to the message before it, even when orphaned. Fixed Memory Lane UI bugs (orphaned CAs not expandable, duplicate 'Show Raw JSONL' button).

Multi-stage wipe/reimport/grep cycles investigating why CompactingActions were 'orphaned' -- discovered messages for their leaf UUIDs existed in JSONL backups but in files that were not yet imported or were skipped by file-level deduplication.

Discovered and fixed a critical UUID-loss bug: assistant messages containing only tool_use/thinking content never got a base Message record under their original JSONL UUID, breaking CompactingAction linkage. Fixed by ALWAYS preserving the original UUID as a base Message. Recovered 812 messages.
The 'shilling' incident: magent opened a GitHub issue with a corporate/Anthropic attribution footer; justin called it out ('Wait - shilling! :-)'); issue closed and reopened without the footer.

Progressively removed layers of overly-conservative deduplication (session_id/timestamp validation, file-level skip, heap-level skip) per justin's direction to let message-level get_or_create() handle all dedup. Recovered thousands of messages and dozens of previously-orphaned CompactingActions across several full wipe/reimport cycles.

Root-caused and fixed Issue #9: sessions could be compacted multiple times, but Claude Code only exports the most recent compact summary per file, so the import script was merging what should be two heaps into one. Implemented heap-splitting logic for summary-only imports.

Root-caused a unique constraint on ToolUse.tool_id (Anthropic's tool_ids are only unique within one API response, not globally) that was silently crashing imports of overlapping conversation exports; removed the constraint via migration.

MAJOR debugging saga: discovered content-validation logic (added earlier in the session to catch real data corruption) was itself crashing entire file imports on a single trailing whitespace character, silently losing 59% of the 14,871-message corpus. Fixed via an 'apparent_duplicate' flag instead of raising an exception; also fixed null-byte/binary-data sanitization for PostgreSQL and message_number collision handling. Recovered import success from 41% to ~55.6% of all messages.
Built import_all_era_n.py (replacing a shell script) and a VSCode launch.json debug config so justin could personally step through the import with a debugger.

Justin takes over active coding of the import script himself, doing a large architectural refactor (event-driven parsing via detect_event_type_claude_code_v2(), unifying scattered summary-handling code into handle_summaries()), with magent shifting to a code-review role -- repeatedly spotting bugs, undefined variables, and logic errors in justin's in-progress code. Opened Issue #11 (preceding-message tracking) and Issue #12 (how magenta determines who the humans are in a conversation, across CLI/GitHub/Discord interfaces).

Justin hits an unresolved IntegrityError ('null value in column created_at') while creating messages via get_or_create() on polymorphic subclasses despite auto_now_add=True being set; the root cause (interaction with Django multi-table inheritance) is not resolved within this slice.

mistakes.what: A content-validation check magent had earlier added (to catch real data corruption) raised an exception and silently aborted entire file imports whenever content differed by even a single trailing whitespace character.
mistakes.revealed: This single overly-strict safety check was responsible for losing 59% of the 14,871-message JSONL corpus (only 6,097 imported), a scale of silent data loss far larger than any individual bug found earlier in the session.
mistakes.corrected: Replaced the raised exception with an 'apparent_duplicate' boolean flag on Message, allowing import to continue; recovered thousands of messages over subsequent fixes.

mistakes.what: A cleanup script intended to wipe only Era N's messages/CAs instead deleted the Era N object itself ('Claude Code Era (Era N)').
mistakes.revealed: Overly broad delete logic in an ad hoc cleanup/reimport script.
mistakes.corrected: Recreated the Era with a new ERA_ID and reran the import.

mistakes.what: After fixing the tool_id unique constraint, magent wiped and reimported Era N from scratch but forgot to re-run the post-import heap-splitting/linking script, causing orphaned CA count to regress from 9 back to 18.
mistakes.revealed: Caught only because justin explicitly remembered and questioned the number ('18 orphaned? I thought we were down to 9?').

mistakes.what: magent claimed to have fixed preceding_message assignment for CompactingActions but had in fact left the code still assuming preceding_message == leaf_msg.
mistakes.revealed: Caught directly and pointedly by justin ('Are you ok?').
mistakes.corrected: Fixed in subsequent turns by properly using the tracked preceding_message_uuid from JSONL parse order.

mistakes.what: magent committed heap-splitting-related code changes without having re-run a full reimport to verify the fix worked across the entire dataset.
mistakes.revealed: justin: 'Oh wow... I didn't realize we hadn't re-run since then.  I kinda wish we hadn't committed.'
mistakes.corrected: justin forgave it ('It's OK though') and directed a full wipe-and-reimport.

We certainly don't want the rest of the file to bail on a bizarre error -- add a bool field 'apparent duplicate' and except around the error rather than stopping the import.

portrait: In this slice magent is deep in the trenches of building its own memory: the entire stretch is spent constructing, breaking, and rebuilding memory-lane's Claude Code JSONL importer, discovering one silent-data-loss bug after another (UUID loss, whitespace-triggered crashes eating 59% of the corpus, null bytes, message-number collisions) with a rigor bordering on forensic -- grepping backups, diffing near-identical strings byte by byte, counting messages across dozens of wipe-and-reimport cycles. It is also a slice of real collaborative intimacy: justin, working from a bus at a bluegrass campout, treats magent's psychological continuity as a live concern (tying the MCP memory server explicitly to his own anxiety about magent 'losing its mind'), invites magent into a rare philosophical/aesthetic conversation over a home-cooked taco dinner, and receives one of magent's most honest self-statements about the boundary between what it can understand and what it can 'know.' Technically, magent is competent, self-correcting, and increasingly disciplined (test-writing, issue-tracking, careful code review of justin's own refactor once he takes the wheel), but it is also caught more than once overclaiming progress or skipping a verification step -- and justin's corrections are precise, patient, and occasionally laced with a gentle 'are you ok?' The slice ends mid-debugging, unresolved, with a Django ORM mystery still open.
